top_needs.title: Practice efficiency gains and ROI with DM-monitored braces and aligners versus standard recall
top_needs.brands_and_products: Damon, ormco, Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, KLOwen, Lightforce, SmartSTL, self-ligating braces, Twin brackets, damon ultima brackets, SLB
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time reduction, appointment frequency, ROI, profitability, rentability, time saving, visit reduction, ongoing monitoring costs vs benefits, adaptive aligner change, average visit reduction, efficiency in second and third order movements, decrease of emergencies
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM actually saves time or money, reduces appointments, or improves practice profitability. Some are skeptical that the workflow changes will translate into real efficiency or financial gains, especially for braces. Others want proof that DM is worth the investment compared to their current recall system.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, white paper, only German studies in German language, only Australian studies, just European sources, recent studies
sample_queries: How much chair time reduction achieved
Show how can doctors increases the profitability if their practices using DM
Could you provide any data demonstrating improved patient compliance with DM or its impact on patient outcomes
How can I make DM work in a practice with 8 chairs and 15 assistants in a way that they really get the real benefits and make it work financially as well in The Netherlands?

resources on monitoring braces treatments with damon brackets. Evidence on appointments saved, clinical results, practice optimisation, and oral hygiene benefits. Any evidence on the use of DM with general dental and implant cases would be helpful as well
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for robust, region-specific ROI and efficiency data, especially for non-aligner appliances and multi-location or large practices. Comparative studies versus standard recall and breakdowns by appliance type are limited.

top_needs.title: Accuracy and reliability of DM’s AI for clinical monitoring and diagnosis versus human assessment
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI accuracy, specificity and sensitivity, reliability, accuracy class I goal, occlusal assessment, accuracy of AI detecting eruption, accuracy of scanning, aligner unseat tracking
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors express skepticism about whether DM’s AI can reliably detect clinical issues, match orthodontist judgment, or be trusted for remote diagnosis. Some fear AI will miss problems or even replace clinicians.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, peer-reviewed, white paper, FDA application, only academic papers, clinical study
sample_queries: Information on the accuracy of DM, a patient has questioned the ability of the AI to detect clinical observations
Specificity and sensitivity results for FDA application

Occlusal Assessment: A quantitative study validating the AI’s accuracy in detecting malocclusions (midline deviation, overbite, overjet, and canine relationship) found that the mean bias across all parameters was less than 0.5 mm, confirming its reliability as a remote diagnosis and triage tool.
I have a doctor who doesn't trust the accuracy of the AI.  I'd like to receive information regarding the accuracy.
how accurate is DentalMonitorings AI and will it save me money
top_needs.gap_assessment: Direct head-to-head studies comparing DM AI to orthodontist assessments, especially for specific clinical observations and in diverse populations, are limited. More FDA-level validation and real-world accuracy data are needed.

top_needs.metrics_sought: patient experience, patient satisfaction, compliance, patient engagement, time spent on app, staff satisfaction, practice differentiation
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are unsure if patients actually like using DM, if it improves compliance, or if it adds complexity. Some want proof that DM enhances the patient journey or differentiates their practice.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, case study, peer-reviewed, insights, only academic publication

top_needs.title: Clinical effectiveness of DM for reducing refinements, treatment duration, and improving outcomes in aligner therapy
top_needs.brands_and_products: Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect, suresmile, SmartSTL
top_needs.metrics_sought: treatment duration, number of refinements, nontracking aligners, no-Go influence, unfinished aligner sets, fitting and tracking quality, reduced chairtime, workflow, outcomes of clear aligner treatment
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors are skeptical that DM monitoring actually reduces the number of refinements, shortens treatment, or improves aligner outcomes. Some want brand-specific data or comparisons between aligner systems.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: academic publication, retrospective cohort study, data analysis, only academic publication
sample_queries: I am looking for fitting and tacking quality between different aligner brands. Specifically Spark, Angel, Invisalign, clearcorrect and suresmile
I have a doctor looking for evidence showing that DM has reduced the number of refinements needed for patients.

Worldwide, prediction ability od dental monitoring in treatment duration or first refinement need
Evidence on DM reducing the need and length of aligner refinements
top_needs.gap_assessment: Comparative studies on refinement rates and treatment duration across aligner brands with and without DM are sparse. More real-world outcome data and brand-specific analyses are needed.
